html:
Brazil is the largest country in South America and the only Portuguese-speaking one in the Americas. It became independent of Portugal in 1822 as an empire, and has been a republic since 1889.

Independence came without a long war. The Portuguese court had moved to Rio de Janeiro in 1808 (see Portuguese court to Brazil). When the king went back to Lisbon, his son Pedro stayed and declared Brazil independent, becoming Emperor Pedro I. This kept the huge former colony of Portuguese Brazil in one piece, unlike Spanish America, which split into many states.

Under his son Pedro II, who reigned from 1831 to 1889, Brazil was fairly stable, and coffee became its great export. But it rested on slavery. Brazil was the last country in the Americas to abolish it, in 1888 (see Brazil abolishes slavery). The next year the army ended the monarchy.

The republic drew millions of immigrants from Italy, Portugal, Spain, Germany and Japan (see Kasato Maru to Brazil). The Amazon rubber boom made fortunes, then collapsed. Getúlio Vargas ruled from 1930 to 1945 and again in the 1950s, building industry and the state. A new capital, Brasília, opened in 1960. A military regime ruled from 1964 to 1985, and democracy returned after it.

Today Brazil has over 210 million people, the largest share of the Amazon rainforest, and the largest population of African descent outside Africa.
sum: Brazil is the largest country in South America and the only Portuguese-speaking one in the Americas. It became independent of Portugal in 1822 as an empire, and has been a republic since 1889.
